newsitem.title: INDIA: India hikes foreign institutional investment limit.
newsitem.headline: India hikes foreign institutional investment limit.

text.p: The Indian government on Friday raised the limit on foreign institutional investors' (FIIs') equity stakes in domestic companies to 30 percent from 24 percent.
The government released a statement announcing that the higher ceiling, proposed in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget, had been implemented.
"The government has notified enhancement of limits on investments by foreign financial investors (FIIs) from 24 percent to 30 percent," the statement said.
Under the new guidelines, FIIs, non-resident Indians and overseas commercial bodies will together be able to hold up to 30 percent of an Indian firm's capital.
Companies which want to allow FIIs to increase their holdings beyond 24 percent need to have the proposal approved by their boards of directors and shareholders.

The government implemented the change although the 1997/98 budget has not been passed and is caught in a political crisis threatening Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who faces a vote of confidence in parliament on April 11.
